subject: Business Models
title: Value Chain Disruption
description: A quick win: understand Value Chain Disruption.

hook.text: Warby Parker cut out middlemen to sell $95 glasses that cost $500 elsewhere. Same quality, different chain.

buildup.text: Traditional eyewear passes through designers, manufacturers, distributors, and retailers. Each adds markup.

discovery.text: By designing, manufacturing, and selling directly, Warby Parker captured all the margin the middlemen took.

twist.text: Luxottica controls 80% of the eyewear market and inflates prices. Warby Parker proved the markup was artificial.

climax.text: Value chain disruption doesn't need new technology. It needs courage to skip the layers everyone assumes are needed.

punchline.text: $95 vs $500 glasses. Same product, fewer middlemen. That's disruption.

quiz.question: How does Warby Parker disrupt the eyewear market?
options: Cutting out middlemen in the value chain

details.summary: Value chain disruption occurs when a new entrant removes, replaces, or reorders steps in the traditional industry value chain. By cutting out intermediaries or integrating previously separate activities, disruptors capture margin that incumbents shared across many players.
details.whyItMatters: Every intermediary in a value chain adds cost and margin. Companies that eliminate unnecessary steps deliver more value at lower prices while capturing the surplus. This is how direct-to-consumer brands and vertical integrators reshape industries.
takeaways: Disruptors remove, replace, or reorder traditional value chain steps
Eliminating intermediaries captures margin previously spread across players
Vertical integration and DTC models are common value chain disruptions

faq.question: What is disintermediation in business model disruption?
faq.answer: Disintermediation removes middlemen from the value chain. When eyeglass maker Warby Parker sells directly to consumers online, it eliminates the wholesale distributor and optical retail chain, capturing their combined margins to offer lower prices.

faq.question: When does value chain disruption fail?
faq.answer: When intermediaries add genuine value that is hard to replicate, such as expert curation, local service, or regulatory compliance. Disruption also fails when the cost of building direct capabilities exceeds savings from cutting out middlemen.
